findings.text: nothing on the live path writes the key this node landed: a review record is written by the review worker's own command, and no brief asks for the emitted REVISION line or for the canonical key (the review prompt that documents the emitted form, reckon/crew/prompts/review.md, is invoked only by tests - load_review_prompt has no production caller), so store_review's canonicalisation fires only when a caller hands it a record carrying one of the five legacy spellings and nothing does: measured, the whole store holds 316 review records and exactly 3 carry reviewed_revision, none of them written on this path, and the 155 reckon records carry whatever their review workers composed, most carrying no revision spelling at all. The second half of the goal (a guard that can tell a review of the current code from a review of a replaced revision) therefore still needs a writer: the prompt line that asks the reviewer to state the revision, and a decision for the 155 existing records that carry no spelling to retrofit.

the canonical key inherits the store's two sha widths and nothing here normalises them, so the follow-on comparison must not test exact equality: measured over the scoped store (316 records, the five spellings carrying 530 non-empty values), 513 values are 40 characters and 17 are 7 or 8 - reviewed_head_sha 6a31b665 beside reviewed_base_sha 780b4f63 in one record, reviewed_commit 7b14e02 and 8891cfa and 6fa99d1 in three others - and _sha_from strips whitespace only, so a review of the current head written as a short sha would read as stale against a 40-character head while being the same revision; the same looseness accepts any text as a revision, so a line 'REVISION: see manifest' is stored as the key's value.

the promoted row still cannot say which revision its review read: ledger_block reduces a stored record to status, scores, absent and total, so the key this node lands is dropped at the boundary promotion writes, and the section's own requirement that whatever consults a review record what it read - the paragraph ending 'recording the figure consulted and the record's modification time on the row makes a later disagreement detectable rather than silent' - remains unmet at the ledger level even with a canonical key in the store; reckon/crew/promotion.py is another node's file, so this is a follow-on rather than an in-scope repair.

the landing record does not link the cumulative evidence anchor it landed in the same commit: the anchor section s5c-revision-canonical-key exists in docs/evidence/archive/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion-landed.html (42 inserted lines, carrying the base/after table and the negative-control table) and the plan page contains zero references to it, so a reader of the landing record cannot reach the numbers - the two sibling records in this section (lines 164 and 1641's neighbours) each link their anchors.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit - c287d2bc carries reckon/crew/review.py (121 insertions, 4 deletions: the canonical key, REVISION_FIELDS, _sha_from, carried_revision, the emitted label set, the parse branch, and store_review's normalisation) plus tests/test_review_records_its_revision.py (168 lines, 32 cases); a1cedc4f carries only documentation - the 42-line evidence anchor, the 33-line landing record, the 130KB figure and its 85-line generator - so nothing else changed and no source path moved in the docs commit.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done-when names one canonical key, all five spellings with their store counts, the absent case, presence-not-truthiness, the falsifier file, the emitted slot and the gate pair with both counts; I reproduced all four numbers in scratch archives of the node's own trees - 32 passed for the falsifier file at c287d2bc, 5 failed / 50 passed for the named pair, 5 failed / 18 passed for tests/test_review_scoring.py at base 9d208d1e, the five failure ids identical between base and head - and reproduced the declared negative control at 5 failed / 27 passed with the same five ids the node's log carries; the one deviation is the PYTHONPATH phrase, read as the root interpreter with PYTHONPATH on the tree under test and documented in the manifest's instrument note, which is the reading that measures the change (the literal one would import the unmodified module).
item_verdicts.goal: the goal asks for one canonical field the parser knows so a guard can compare a verdict's revision against the code being promoted; reckon/crew/review.py:108-166 lands reviewed_revision with a documented precedence (head spellings over base, sha over commit list) resolved by key presence, reckon/crew/review.py:376-382 attaches it to every parsed record from the emitted text or a supplied record, and reckon/crew/review.py:439-442 normalises a stored record before it is written - all three halves in place, but no runtime caller writes the key today (finding 1), so the capability is complete and the writer is not.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records both commits with their shas, the five declared paths, the focused gate at both ends with log paths, an armed baseline/after pair whose five failure ids I reproduced, and a negative control whose first line repeats the declared mutation verbatim; its status is a recognised terminal value and its checkpoint names where the work stands; the one field that does not hold is the stated convention that a gate log's first line names the revision, the tree and the command - neither gate-base.log nor gate-head.log carries a header, their first line is the pytest progress line, so the tree is recoverable only from the paths inside the log and the revision is not stated at all.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read against git diff --numstat 9d208d1e..c287d2bc (121/4 reckon/crew/review.py, 168/0 tests/test_review_records_its_revision.py - exactly the two declared code paths and nothing else) and c287d2bc..a1cedc4f (42/0 evidence anchor, 33/0 plan record, 85/0 figure generator, one binary figure - the three declared docs paths), and the target worktree is clean at a1cedc4f with no untracked paths.

justifications.durability: tests/test_review_records_its_revision.py asserts all five spellings through both the parser and the store, the absent case in both, the presence-not-truthiness fork, the precedence of the emitted line over a supplied record, and that the legacy spelling survives beside the canonical key; the declared mutation (key presence replaced by truthiness in carried_revision; "if field in record:" becomes "if record.get(field):") reddens exactly those assertions when I applied it to a scratch copy of c287d2bc - 5 failed / 27 passed, the same five ids as the node's log - so the assertions can fail, and the store write was verified by reading the record back rather than by trusting the write.
justifications.evidence: every count reproduces under my own instrument: 32 passed for the falsifier file, 5 failed / 50 passed for the named pair, 5 failed / 18 passed for the scoring file at base, identical five failure ids (diff of the FAILED lines is empty), negative control 5 failed / 27 passed with the same ids; the write scope is exact by numstat and the worktree is clean; the deductions are the gate logs' missing header - the manifest's own convention asks the first line to name the revision, the tree and the command, and neither log names any - and the landing record's unlinked evidence anchor.
justifications.fit: the names state the mechanism (REVIEW_REVISION_KEY, REVISION_FIELDS, carried_revision, _sha_from) and the comments carry the why rather than the change history; the module's existing idioms are mirrored (the same falsifier-with-negative-control style, the store's atomic rename untouched), and the one looseness is that the emitted label match accepts any value for the key, which the section's census-style discipline would normally bound (reported as finding 2).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is met as a capability and defeated only at the writer: reviewed_revision resolves from each of the five store spellings by key presence, a spelling carried empty stays a recorded absence while no spelling leaves the key absent, the emitted form gains a slot, and store_review normalises before writing while preserving the legacy spellings; what no code path does is write the key into a record on the live path, so the guard the section promises still cannot compare anything until a writer and the comparison land (finding 1).
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --numstat 9d208d1e..c287d2bc lists exactly the two declared code paths and c287d2bc..a1cedc4f exactly the three declared documentation paths plus the figure generator, all insertions-only on the docs side; the worktree is clean; the plan's meta lines and other sections are untouched, and no concurrent node's path was written.
